__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus (debvulns exporter)
__inputs.description: Prometheus datasource scraping one or more debvulns-exporter instances

description: Debian package vulnerability monitoring for deployatnight/debvulns (Go) exporter. Blocks: Scanner Health (data trust) -> Exposure KPIs + trend -> Act Now (remediation mapping Installed Version -> Fix Version) -> Inventory & Fleet. NOTE: the EPSS Data Health panel is a heuristic (all-zero EPSS detection) until the exporter ships a dedicated debvulns_epss_status metric.

panels.title: Scanner Health — can I trust the data?
Scan Status
panels.description: 1 = last scan succeeded on ALL selected instances (min across fleet). 0 = scan failed; the dashboard may still show a retained last-good snapshot. Matches alert DebvulnsScanFailed.

panels.title: Scan Age (oldest instance)
panels.description: Time since the oldest successful scan across selected instances. Default refresh-interval is 24h: green < 8h, yellow < 24h, red >= 24h (stale feed = blind to new CVEs). Matches alert DebvulnsNoScanReporting.

panels.title: EPSS Data Health (heuristic)
panels.description: Heuristic until the exporter exposes debvulns_epss_status: 1 = every selected instance has nonzero EPSS scores for all its CVEs; 0 = EPSS data missing (all scores silently zeroed — the exporter keeps scan_status=1 on EPSS download failure) or some CVEs genuinely score 0. If SUSPECT, do not trust EPSS-based ordering in 'Patch Now' / tables.

panels.title: Instances Reporting
panels.description: Number of selected instances currently exposing debvulns_exporter_info. Combined with 'Scan Age' this distinguishes 'no data' from 'no vulnerabilities'.

panels.title: Affected Packages (selected severity)
panels.description: Installed packages carrying at least one CVE in the severities selected by the $severity variable (package × instance pairs). Each pair is one 'apt upgrade' target. Ignores negligible by default to keep signal above noise.

panels.title: Unique CVEs (fleet-wide)
panels.description: Distinct CVE identifiers across selected instances within the selected severities. A CVE affecting N hosts counts once — this is the size of the analysis backlog, not the patching workload.

panels.title: Crit/High — Fix Available
panels.description: Distinct critical/high CVEs for which Debian already released a patch (independent of the $severity variable). 0 = green. Anything above zero belongs on the remediation worklist below.

panels.title: Crit/High — No Fix Yet
panels.description: Distinct critical/high CVEs without a Debian patch (fix_available="false"). These cannot be closed by apt upgrade — track upstream, vendor advisories or apply compensating controls. Matches alert DebvulnsRemoteExploitableNoFix when remote=true.

panels.title: Vulnerability Trend by Severity
panels.description: Fleet-wide vulnerability counts per derived severity over time. Downward steps = packages patched or removed; upward steps = new CVEs published or new packages installed. This is the only panel using the pre-aggregated debvulns_vulnerabilities_total metric.

panels.title: Severity Distribution (current)
panels.description: Current fleet-wide counts by derived severity. Severity is computed by the exporter from Debian urgency + EPSS: critical = urgency high AND EPSS > 0.3; high = urgency high OR EPSS > 0.5; medium = urgency medium OR EPSS > 0.1; low / negligible = the rest.

panels.title: Patch Now — High EPSS, Fix Available
panels.description: Top 10 critical/high (cve, package) pairs by EPSS exploitation probability where Debian already released a patch. EPSS > 0.5 means realistic near-term exploitation risk. Patch these first — the table below gives the exact target versions.

targets.expr: topk(10, debvulns_vulnerability_epss_score{instance=~"$instance"} * on(cve, package, instance) group_left() (debvulns_vulnerability_info{instance=~"$instance", severity=~"critical|high", fix_available="true"}))

panels.title: Monitor — High EPSS, No Fix Yet
panels.description: Top 10 critical/high (cve, package) pairs by EPSS with no Debian patch available. Cannot be closed by apt upgrade — subscribe to Debian security advisories for the source package, consider backports or compensating controls.

targets.expr: topk(10, debvulns_vulnerability_epss_score{instance=~"$instance"} * on(cve, package, instance) group_left() (debvulns_vulnerability_info{instance=~"$instance", severity=~"critical|high", fix_available="false"}))

panels.title: Remediation Plan — Fix Available (Installed → Fix Version)
panels.description: The remediation worklist: every vulnerable (cve, package) pair with a released Debian patch, mapped from the currently installed version to the fix version to upgrade to. Built from the 4-way join epss_score × vulnerability_info × package_info × fix_info. Sorted by Severity, then EPSS desc. Respects the $severity filter.

panels.title: No Fix Yet — Track Upstream
panels.description: Vulnerable (cve, package) pairs with no Debian patch (Fix Version is empty). Prioritise Remote = YES rows and high EPSS. Verify the 'EPSS Data Health' panel is OK before trusting EPSS ordering here — the exporter silently zeroes scores when the EPSS feed download fails.

panels.title: Vulnerability Details (full inventory)
panels.description: Complete fact table: all active (cve, package) pairs enriched with EPSS, derived severity, Debian urgency, remediation flags and both versions. Select 'negligible' in the $severity variable to see the long tail (typically thousands of rows).

panels.title: Top Packages by CVE Count
panels.description: Packages ranked by number of distinct CVEs in the selected severities. One 'apt upgrade <package>' here clears many findings at once — the cheapest remediation lever. Respects the $severity filter.

panels.title: Fleet Matrix — which host to patch first
panels.description: One row per instance: Debian suite, exporter version, installed package count, affected packages (all severities, including negligible) and unique critical/high CVEs. Built by joining four queries on the instance label.

list.description: Derived severity (Debian urgency + EPSS) applied to the tables and KPI stats. Negligible is excluded by default to keep signal above noise.
list.label: Severity
list.name: severity
